ui.about.db.intro: The site’s data layers (the Ministry of Education list, ShanghaiRanking GRAS, Sino-foreign joint programmes, the Hong Kong／Macao／Taiwan pool, overseas institutions, origin-branch official pages, programmes and subject requirements, admission channels, direct-hire programmes) are unified into one static database with versions, sources and validity periods, readable by sister products (path, gk) and anyone else: {institutions} institutions, {crosswalk} cross-layer links, {channels} admission channels, {conditions} indexed conditions, {sources} sources (each with an authority tier), {validity} validity records; large files (per-school programme lists, overseas verbatim quotes) are not copied but referenced by URL and SHA-256.
ui.about.db.links: Entry point: <a1>/db/v1/latest.json ↗</a1> (points to the current version {version}; version directories never change) · usage contract: <a2>docs/DB_API.md ↗</a2> · field definitions: <a3>docs/DB_SCHEMA.md ↗</a3> · annual update: <a4>docs/ANNUAL_UPDATE.md ↗</a4>
ui.about.db.rule: The database is only a unified index of existing data with source and validity notes, not a recommendation; rankings only describe subject distribution; only sources marked linkable should be rendered as links.
ui.about.db.title: Read-only open database
ui.about.dims.A: A · Red lines (6 questions): province, city tier, institutional tier, tuition band, campus location. One strike and it is out; unknown campus or exact fees stay unknown.
ui.about.dims.B: B · Campus life (24 questions): dorms, air conditioning, showers, study sessions, morning runs, food delivery, power cuts, hot water, curfews and more. Crowd-sourced; missing stays missing, nothing is assumed. Anonymous reports lack campus and year, so they are shown but never exclude a whole school.
ui.about.dims.C: C · Special (5 questions): dietary restrictions, accessibility, LGBTQ+, out-of-province share, discipline evaluation.
ui.about.dims.E: E · Environment (8 questions): central heating, summer and winter feel, smog, dialect, metro, coast, altitude. Derived objectively from province + city using China Meteorological Administration, Ministry of Ecology and Environment and China Association of Metros data; covers every school.
ui.about.dims.note: The questionnaire adapts to current data coverage. Questions or options that cannot actually remove any school are hidden for now, so you don’t answer in vain. Hiding has a cost: a question could quietly lose half its options, so the repository has an audit gate: any value that exists in the enumeration but not in the data must be declared explicitly, or the build fails.
ui.about.dims.title: Four kinds of dimension (42 base dimensions)
ui.about.language.text: The interface is available in Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese and English. The Simplified version is generated from the Traditional source by character-level script conversion with no change of vocabulary; official names (schools, programmes, institutions, source titles) stay in their original form, neither translated nor converted. The English version is this site’s own translation; where they differ, the Traditional Chinese text prevails. Your language choice is stored only in this browser and never enters any learning record.
ui.about.language.title: Languages
ui.about.method.derivation: Authoritative derivation is the exception: geographic facts such as province → climate, dialect or coast come from authoritative bodies and are not assumptions.
ui.about.method.evidence: Evidence-scope threshold: anonymous campus-life reports keep the full response count and the votes for each answer; unclassifiable does not mean non-existent, and mixed votes from different campuses are never treated as school-wide policy. Only official, current-year, school-wide data can exclude; campus-level data is for reference.
ui.about.method.neutral: Neutral presentation: every dimension is shown as fact + timestamp + source.
ui.about.method.noAdvice: No application advice, no indication of admission chances: this site is not an educational institution and is not responsible for admission outcomes.
ui.about.method.noDefault: No assumptions: no school-level field is filled from inferences like “985 universities usually have this”. Missing stays missing, and users are invited to contribute.
ui.about.method.nonCommercial: Non-commercial: this is a non-commercial public-interest site; data derived from CollegesChat inherits CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
ui.about.method.presumption: Benefit of the doubt: when a school has no data on a dimension, that question never excludes it.
ui.about.method.prior: A prior is not a conclusion: most schools admit on filed preferences alone, so that is the default; but the default must be overridable by the charter. Institutions whose undergraduate admission is only through comprehensive evaluation (separate registration + school test) are recorded per province and year in the admission-channel table, tagged “comprehensive evaluation · no regular batch” next to the name, with the charter linked. Where no charter is found, the default stands: better to exclude too little than to exclude wrongly.
ui.about.method.title: Methodology
ui.about.roadmap.global: Global subtraction: Hong Kong / Macao / Taiwan and overseas starting points subtract over the overseas layer and the pool by region, subject and channel type; unknowns stay, qualifications only label, every crossed-out institution shows why; choices stay on this device and out of the learning record, and a Hong Kong / Macao / Taiwan institution may count once in each pool.
ui.about.roadmap.intro: First where you are studying, then subtraction step by step; students can choose across borders, and non-university paths such as direct hiring are included.
ui.about.roadmap.link: Full goals and source tiers: <a1>project document ↗</a1>
ui.about.roadmap.s0: Mainland China: a subtraction bank over every regular institution in the Ministry of Education 2026 list, with programmes and subject requirements.
ui.about.roadmap.s1: World subject atlas: leading institutions per subject in ShanghaiRanking GRAS 2026, crossed out by subject and region; plus employer programmes that hire high-school graduates.
ui.about.roadmap.s2: Hong Kong / Macao / Taiwan pool: each institution’s official admission channels and the official routes into mainland universities; Sino-foreign programmes appear on school pages.
ui.about.roadmap.s3: Overseas institutions: official admissions page text for {institutions} non-mainland institutions and the application platforms and visa pages of {regions} countries and regions; anything unread is labelled as such.
ui.about.roadmap.s45: Languages and read-only database: Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese and English; the /db/v1 database is described below.
ui.about.roadmap.title: Coverage
ui.about.scope.counts: Under the Ministry of Education’s 2026 scope there are {total} regular institutions; the {adult} adult institutions are noted for scope only and are not in the filtering pool.
ui.about.scope.curated: Manually curated fields currently cover a small number of key schools, adding English names, campus types and a few high-value samples; they are not the official master list.
ui.about.scope.title: Scope and missing data

ui.about.sources.overseasLayer: · Overseas institutions (#/overseas): the {institutions} non-mainland institutions in the global subject atlas. Starting from the official websites already verified, a crawler that identifies itself, respects robots.txt and never logs in or bypasses verification read each university’s official international undergraduate admissions page (at most 16 pages per university, staying on the same official domain), quoting excerpts verbatim (Gaokao recognition, accepted qualifications, English and other language requirements, international tuition, application channels, timelines, academic year) with the source URL and fetch date; no interpretation, no conversion, no AI-generated text. It also verified {portals} official national application platforms / information portals and {visa} visa authority pages. Official pages were read for {verified} institutions ({high} on the same official domain, {medium} on another official domain of the school); {blocked} served a verification page to the identified crawler or disallow it in robots.txt, {notFound} had no matching page, and {needsReview} are JavaScript-only and await manual review. Link rule: an institution’s admissions page is linked only when read on the same official domain, another official domain awaits manual confirmation; a non-government platform shared by many universities is linked only when an institution’s official page links to it; visa pages are linked only when read; where blocked, only the authority’s name and “blocked during verification” are shown. The data is re-checked with each GRAS update. Method and per-institution evidence: docs/MAINTENANCE_MANUAL.md §3.7 ↗

ui.about.tiers.intro: Every outbound link on this site is tiered by who owns the target and labelled next to the link; the tier describes the domain, not whether the page is reachable today.
ui.about.tiers.p0: Official (P0): governments, education authorities and the bodies directly under them (including the Ministry of Education degree centre’s discipline evaluation), official examination bodies, institution websites and admissions offices, programme pages on a company’s own domain or on the organiser’s dedicated programme site.
ui.about.tiers.p1: Authoritative platform (P1): platforms commissioned or authorised by an authority, or with a published methodology that this site uses only descriptively — the Yangguang Gaokao platform, ShanghaiRanking GRAS, the Taiwan joint admission committees, industry-association statistics, third-party recruiting systems hosting official vacancies.
ui.about.tiers.p2: Third party (P2): media reports, open-source communities and crowd-sourced data; corroboration or a contribution entry point only, never an authority.
ui.about.tiers.rule: Rankings and third-party data only describe distribution and are never a basis for recommendation. Links are rechecked yearly with the ranking update: anything that fails is not published and is shown as text with the reason; an official page that serves a verification page to a declared checker does not count as unreachable; a mainland university site is marked “temporarily unreachable” only after two consecutive failed rounds (<a1>annual check rules ↗</a1>).
ui.about.tiers.title: Source authority tiers
ui.about.useful.text: Share the site with seniors, current students and alumni who know different schools. Every verifiable addition leaves one less blank in the questionnaire and brings it closer to a tool that truly helps people subtract.
ui.about.useful.title: If you find it useful
ui.about.why.p1: Almost every application tool tells you “where to apply”. We don’t. We only help you cross out the ones you can’t stand, so the sieve goes from the {total} regular institutions on the Ministry of Education’s 2026 list down to the few hundred that remain.
ui.about.why.p2: What remains is not “what we recommend”; it is “what you have no reason to exclude”. The judgement always stays with you.
ui.about.why.title: Why subtract?

ui.channels.hk.dse.summary: No separate exam: apply with the year’s HKDSE results (Hong Kong identity card plus Home Return Permit or residence permit); online registration around March. The 2026 measures state: minimum standard “3, 3, 2, A” (level 3 or above in Chinese Language and English Language, level 2 or above in Mathematics, “attained” in Citizenship and Social Development; arts and sports programmes “2, 2, 1, A”); Principal Recommendation Scheme: Citizenship and Social Development attained and the other three core subjects totalling at least 8 with no subject below 2, 8 per school; up to 4 institutions with 4 programmes each; outside the national regular admission quota; fees equal to mainland students in the same programme. Education Bureau press release: 165 mainland institutions admit Hong Kong students for 2026/27 (the 2023 list had 132). Older measures said “Liberal Studies”; it is now Citizenship and Social Development; the year’s measures prevail.
ui.channels.hk.dse.title: Scheme for Admission of Hong Kong Students to Mainland Higher Education Institutions (HKDSE-based)
ui.channels.hk.joint.summary: 2026 prospectus (values at the time): registration 1–31 March (online 1–15 March); examination 23–24 May; science track Chinese, Mathematics, English, Physics, Chemistry and humanities track Chinese, Mathematics, English, History, Geography, 150 marks each; seven examination districts including Hong Kong (HKEAA International and Professional Examinations Division) and Macao; parallel preferences of 10 institutions with 6 programmes each; admission in early July; fees equal to mainland students in the same programme.
ui.channels.hk.joint.title: National Joint Admission for Overseas Chinese, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan Students
ui.channels.mo.baosong.summary: Run on recommendation by the Ministry of Education’s Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan Affairs Office and the Macao Education and Youth Development Bureau; the bureau’s page loads only by JavaScript, so this site could not read the official page and, by rule, shows no link pending manual review.
ui.channels.mo.baosong.title: Recommendation-based admission of Macao students to mainland universities
ui.channels.mo.jae.summary: Example: Central China Normal University’s 2021 prospectus (the page exists; the text is an attachment this site did not read). Whether it still runs, and on what terms, follows each university’s prospectus for the year.
ui.channels.mo.jae.title: Admission on Macao four-university joint-exam results (run by individual universities)
ui.channels.mo.joint.summary: 2026 prospectus (values at the time): registration 1–31 March (online 1–15 March); examination 23–24 May; 150 marks per subject; the Macao examination district is run by the Education and Youth Development Bureau; parallel preferences of 10 institutions with 6 programmes each; admission in early July; fees equal to mainland students in the same programme.
ui.channels.mo.joint.title: National Joint Admission for Overseas Chinese, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan Students

ui.channels.title: Official channels into mainland universities
ui.channels.tw.gsat.summary: 2023 measures (values at the time): Taiwan residence permit or Mainland Travel Permit plus valid proof of residence in Taiwan; eligible once any one of Chinese, Mathematics (A or B) or English in the year’s GSAT reaches the “average standard” benchmark or above; registration in March (free); up to 6 institutions with 6 programmes each; universities may add a written test or interview based on at most four GSAT subjects; provisional admission published mid-May with a second round of preferences in late May; fees equal to mainland students in the same programme. The application system page is a login page this site did not read, so it is not linked.
ui.channels.tw.gsat.title: Admission of Taiwan high-school graduates on GSAT scores
ui.channels.tw.joint.summary: Taiwan candidates: Mainland Travel Permit or residence permit plus valid proof of residence in Taiwan; none of the seven examination districts is in Taiwan, so candidates sit the exam in Beijing, Shanghai, Zhejiang, Fujian, Guangdong, Hong Kong or Macao. Otherwise as in the 2026 prospectus (values at the time).
ui.channels.tw.joint.title: National Joint Admission for Overseas Chinese, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan Students
